title: Uncertainty Quantification for Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Heydar Soudani; Hamed Zamani; Faegheh Hasibi
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Uncertainty in RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a UQ method for retrieval-augmented reasoning that captures uncertainty from both retriever and generator, and applies it to abstention and model selection—directly relevant to calibration/control and uncertainty under unreliable evidence.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
authors: Baolong Bi; Shenghua Liu; Yiwei Wang; Yilong Xu; Junfeng Fang; Lingrui Mei; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes CK-PLUG, a decoding-time method to control LLM reliance on parametric vs retrieved knowledge using entropy-based confidence gain to detect conflicts, directly addressing knowledge conflict and calibration/control in RAG.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
authors: Xin Sun; Jianan Xie; Zhongqi Chen; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Yuehe Chen; Bowen Song; Weiqiang Wang; Zilei Wang; Liang Wang
why_relevant: Proposes DPO-based alignment for RAG to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries, directly addressing calibration, abstention, and noisy retrieval robustness.

title: ATM: Adversarial Tuning Multi-agent System Makes a Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generator
why_relevant: ATM proposes adversarial multi-agent tuning to make RAG generators robust against fabricated/noisy retrieved documents, directly addressing robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Understanding Data Poisoning Attacks for RAG: Insights and Algorithms
why_relevant: Proposes both a new defense (DRS) and stealthier attack against data poisoning of RAG retrieval corpora, directly addressing adversarial corruption robustness.

title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yikun Han; Mengfei Lan; Halil Kilicoglu
why_relevant: Studies RAG under conflicting biomedical evidence, examining order effects, calibration, and proposing a conflict-aware abstention score. Directly addresses knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and selective prediction.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and uses an existing benchmark.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
authors: Shrey Shah; Levent Ozgur
why_relevant: Introduces a controlled benchmark for evaluating web agents/RAG under adversarial ranking with misinformation, measuring accuracy collapse, search escalation, and miscalibration—directly relevant to robustness, conflict, and calibration themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on web agents rather than pure RAG pipelines, but threat model and findings transfer.

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hua Ye; Siyuan Chen; Ziqi Zhong; Canran Xiao; Haoliang Zhang; Yuhan Wu; Fei Shen
why_relevant: Proposes a framework for detecting and resolving context-memory conflicts in RAG via interpretable signals (semantic match, factual consistency, self-answerability), directly addressing knowledge conflict and confidence-aware control.

title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents
authors: Ishrith Gowda
why_relevant: Formalizes memory poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented agents as a Stackelberg game and proposes MEMSAD, a calibration-based anomaly detection defense with certified detection radius and minimax optimality guarantees. Directly addresses adversarial corruption of RAG memory and calibration-based defenses.

title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective
authors: Lu Dai; Liang Sun; Fanpu Cao; Ziyang Rao; Cehao Yang; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
why_relevant: A perspective/survey paper on denoising across the RAG pipeline, covering noise sensitivity, prompt injection, verifiability, and context engineering—directly aligned with the survey's scope.

title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights
authors: Yi Chen; Daiwei Chen; Sukrut Madhav Chikodikar; Caitlyn Heqi Yin; Ramya Korlakai Vinayak
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates conformal factuality filtering for RAG, showing fragility under distribution shifts and distractors, and proposes informativeness-aware metrics—directly addressing calibration, robustness, and evaluation of RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
authors: Yibo Zhao; Jiapeng Zhu; Zichen Ding; Xiang Li
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Grounding
why_relevant: GRACE is an RL framework that jointly trains an RAG model to ground answers in evidence and abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, directly addressing calibration/abstention and unreliable evidence handling.

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
authors: Tianzhe Zhao; Jiaoyan Chen; Shuxiu Zhang; Haiping Zhu; Qika Lin; Jun Liu
why_relevant: Introduces ConflictQA, a benchmark for cross-source knowledge conflicts (text vs KG) in RAG, plus an explanation-based method (XoT) to mitigate evidence bias. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and evaluation under unreliable evidence.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Sunguk Shin; Meeyoung Cha; Byung-Jun Lee; Sungwon Park
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention under Knowledge Conflict
why_relevant: ERA directly addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence, uses evidential deep learning and Dempster-Shafer theory to calibrate confidence, and enables abstention under unsupported queries — central themes of the survey.

title: Cordon-MAS: Defending RAG against Knowledge Poisoning via Information-Flow Control
authors: Zhe Yu; Wenpeng Xing; Gaolei Li; Shuguang Xiong; Hongzhi Wang; Xuyang Teng; Meng Han
why_relevant: Proposes an architectural multi-agent defense against RAG knowledge poisoning, framing it as an information-flow control problem and showing a monitoring-control gap in LLMs handling poisoned evidence.

title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Wentao Zhang; Yan Zhuang; ZhuHang Zheng; Mingfei Zhang; Jiawen Deng; Fuji Ren
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Jamming Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes a novel soft-failure jamming attack on RAG via adversarial document injection, exploiting safety alignment to induce non-informative answers while evading detection. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and availability threats in RAG.

title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning
authors: Samuel Korn
why_relevant: Evaluates four RAG architectures against adversarial knowledge base poisoning under N=1 settings, decomposing retrieval- vs generation-stage vulnerabilities and introducing a behavioral taxonomy capturing contradiction detection and hedging.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qingying Niu; Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Bohui Fang; Wayne Xin Zhao
why_relevant: ArbGraph directly addresses conflict resolution and noise suppression in RAG by arbitrating evidence credibility through a conflict-aware graph before generation, targeting retrieved-vs-retrieved conflicts and noisy long-form RAG.
